title: Introduce transactional stream sessions and credential stability helpers (v1.2.4)
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context & motivation: Customers have run into intermittent stream failures when credentials are rotated mid-stream and when applying at-least-once semantics for multi-request transactions over streaming connections. This PR adds a small, idiomatic Go surface for transactional stream sessions (SessionManager + TransactionalStream) and a set of credential-stability helpers that reduce mid-stream auth churn. The goal is pragmatic: make long-lived streaming consumers easier to reason about and reduce transient 401s during credential handoffs without altering server-side auth semantics.

Summary of changes (high level):
- Add session.Transaction and session.Manager types to manage transactional boundaries over streams and allow client-side checkpointing and idempotent retries.
- Introduce cred.StableProvider and cred.WrapWithLease(ctx, provider, leaseDuration) helper to hold a short-lived credential window and perform prefetching/refresh handoffs.
- Add engineered backoff presets for stream reconnects when using transactional sessions (stream-friendly exponential + jitter + bounded growth).
- Expose streamingHeartbeats config option in client.NewStream to keep server-side sessions warm.
- Minor ergonomics: chainable WithTransaction(ctx, opts...) builder pattern and clearer typed errors for stream cancellation vs auth failures.
- Version bump: go-sdk v1.2.4 (module patch), release notes added.

Commits (summary):
- 8a3f2b3: feat(session): add Transaction, Manager, and checkpoint API with documentation comments
- 1b7d4c1: feat(cred): implement StableProvider + lease wrapper and unit tests for concurrent refresh
- dea9e01: feat(stream): add streamingHeartbeats option and reconnect backoff presets; update NewStream signature
- c2f4b8a: refactor(api): chainable WithTransaction builder and typed stream errors; update examples
- 44e5a6f: test: add integration test that simulates mid-stream credential rotation and asserts graceful refresh
- 9f0b3d2: ci: add flaky test retry for stream integration on slower CI workers; bump go-sdk to v1.2.4

Files changed (high level):
- client/stream.go (new option + heartbeat wiring)
- session/manager.go (new package: transactional session manager)
- session/transaction.go (transactional boundary API)
- cred/stable_provider.go (new helper + lease wrapper)
- cred/stable_provider_test.go (concurrency and refresh tests)
- examples/streams/transactional-readme.go (usage example)
- go.mod, go.sum (version bump)
- docs/sdk/go/release-notes-1.2.4.md (release notes snippet)

Why this is different from previous work: Existing PRs focused on credential fallback, session bridges, and stream backoff profiles but mostly address either short-lived session ergonomics or SDK-side retry adapters. This change stitches three concerns together specifically for long-lived transactional streaming consumers: explicit transactional boundaries, a lease-based cred handoff that reduces mid-stream auth races, and backoff profiles tuned for transactionality (so retries are less likely to produce duplicates). The API intentionally favors explicit checkpoints to make idempotency and auditing straightforward.

Testing & CI:
- Unit tests cover the StableProvider refresh race, Transaction checkpoint lifecycle, and typed error conversions.
- Integration test (integration/streams/rotate-credentials) runs in a sandbox harness that simulates a credential rotation event during an active transaction and verifies no dropped writes and at-most-once checkpoint application semantics.
- Local benchmark shows ~2% overhead when using StableProvider vs naive provider (measured on developer workstation with 16 clients multiplexed into a single stream).
- CI: final status PASS after re-running the flaky stream integration twice on slow workers.

Backward compatibility and migration notes:
- Default behavior is unchanged: existing NewStream callers will not see different auth semantics unless they opt into StableProvider or transaction APIs.
- For teams that want immediate protection against mid-stream 401s, replace provider with cred.WrapWithLease(ctx, provider, 15s) in the short term.
- TransactionalSession APIs are additive. We created small adapter helpers to let existing Stream consumers adopt checkpoints incrementally.

Checklist: 
- [x] Unit tests 
- [x] Integration test 
- [x] Benchmarks 
- [x] Docs + release notes 
- [x] Version bump to v1.2.4

Related work / tickets: Linear: ENG-7421, ENG-7523; Incident: SUP-1184 (mid-stream 401 during heavy load)

Additional notes: This PR purposefully avoids server-side protocol changes; all work is client-side and intended to be safe to roll out incrementally. The credential lease wrapper can be used across SDKs but is implemented here for Go first; follow-up tasks are in the Linear backlog to port parity to Python/TS if this proves effective in customer environments.
release_notes: Add transactional stream sessions (SessionManager + Transaction APIs) and StableProvider credential lease helper; streaming heartbeat option; backoff presets tuned for transactions. Backwards-compatible. SDK patch release v1.2.4.

review_conversation: Diego: Can we make the lease duration configurable per Stream? Suggest adding an option to NewStream; also call out how this interacts with provider caching.\nMaya: Added streaming option and documented interaction with provider caches; default lease is 15s and can be overridden via WithStableLease().

Priya: Unit tests look good but integration failed on first run (timeout). Is this test flakey?\nMaya: The integration depends on CI worker timing; added a short retry around harness startup and increased timeouts for slower CI nodes; re-ran and passed.

Samir: API ergonomics look clean, but ensure errors returned on failed checkpoint application are typed so callers can decide to retry or abort.\nMaya: Introduced ErrCheckpointConflict and ErrAuthDuringCheckpoint typed errors; updated docs with guidance.
notes_for_release_manager: Ship as go-sdk v1.2.4. Call out the new StableProvider helper in the release notes and examples; recommend including a short migration blurb for teams using long-lived streams. Monitor SUP-1184 for residual reports after rollout.
